Santalum album

Indian sandalwood, from legally harvested plantation timber.

Soft, milky and persistent — the standard every other wood is measured against. Santalum album is slow-growing and tightly regulated, which is why real Indian sandalwood costs what it does and why so much of what is sold under the name is not this species at all.

How to use

  • Warm a single drop between the palms and inhale before meditation.
  • Dilute to 1% as a face oil for dry or reactive skin.
  • Add one drop to rose or jasmine to hold the floral note for longer.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Scent profile

  • Creamy wood
  • Warm milk
  • Soft balsam

What's in it

Who it's for

Meditation practice

The oil with the deepest association with this use in India, and still bought mostly for it.

Dry or reactive skin

Long used in facial oils at low dilution, and one of the gentler materials on skin.

Serious blenders

A base note that holds florals in place better than almost anything else available.

What people get wrong

Assuming any oil labelled sandalwood is this species. Australian sandalwood, Amyris and West Indian sandalwood are all sold under the name and are a fraction of the price for good reason. Check for Santalum album.

Using too much. This is the most expensive thing we sell by volume and a single drop carries. Treating it like cedarwood is an expensive habit.

What it won't do

Santalum album is slow-growing and tightly regulated in India, which constrains how much legally harvested oil exists. We buy small quantities and sell a 5 ml bottle because that is what we can supply honestly.

If you have bought cheap sandalwood before and liked the smell, this may not match it — most inexpensive sandalwood is a different species or a synthetic reconstruction.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Sandalwood

Why is it this expensive?

Santalum album takes decades to develop usable heartwood, harvesting is tightly regulated in India, and demand far exceeds supply. Any Indian sandalwood oil priced cheaply is almost certainly not Santalum album.

Is it legally and sustainably sourced?

It comes from regulated plantation timber rather than wild harvest, through suppliers who can document it. We buy in small quantities and would rather run out than take a volume we cannot stand behind.

How is this different from Australian sandalwood?

Australian sandalwood is Santalum spicatum, a related but distinct species. It is drier, slightly greener and considerably cheaper. It is a legitimate oil in its own right, but it is not Indian sandalwood.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Around 2% for the body — roughly 12 drops per 30 ml of carrier oil — and 1% for the face. Always patch-test before wider use, and never apply neat.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
